title: SCALE: Style-Causal Disentanglement with Adaptive Lifelong Expert for Online Latent-domain Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Online anomaly detection must handle evolving operating conditions in streams where domain labels and shift times are unobserved, domains may grow over time, and adaptation and detection must occur in a single pass.

gap.claim: Existing stream settings can mistake distribution shifts for anomalies, motivating online latent-domain anomaly detection under unobserved and growing domains.

contributions.claim: SCALE disentangles each window into domain-invariant causal features and domain-specific style features.
SCALE supports continual adaptation with a dynamically expandable style-expert pool and uses separate criteria for drift identification and final anomaly scoring.
The paper establishes theoretical properties concerning drift detection and distinguishing domain shifts from true anomalies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report theoretical properties showing that SLR reliably detects domain drift and, together with CPR, further distinguishes domain shift from true anomalies.
The authors report extensive experiments on diverse real-world datasets.
The authors report a new multi-domain time-series anomaly detection benchmark for evaluating online latent-domain scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Evolving operating conditions make distribution shifts difficult to distinguish from anomalies in real-world time-series streams.
The paper formulates online latent-domain anomaly detection with unobserved domains and shift times, potentially growing domains, and single-pass adaptation and detection.
SCALE combines style-causal disentanglement, an expandable style-expert pool, and separate drift-identification and anomaly-scoring criteria.
The paper reports theoretical analysis, experiments on diverse real-world datasets, and a new multi-domain benchmark.

source_observation.claim: Distribution shifts can be mistaken for anomalies when operating conditions evolve.

interpretation.claim: An anomaly detector should model changing context separately from abnormal behavior.

application.claim: For streaming detection systems, consider separate mechanisms for identifying drift and scoring anomalies.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this separation works beyond the reported datasets and benchmark.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architecture or training procedure.
The abstract does not report quantitative experimental results, baselines, or dataset names.
The abstract does not describe the assumptions or proof details underlying the theoretical properties.
